profile.campus: Ashburn, Loudoun County, Virginia (Equinix Ashburn campus, Data Center Alley)
profile.address: 21701 Filigree Court, Building D, Ashburn, VA 20147
profile.reading: This building is Equinix's DC5 facility on Equinix's Ashburn, Virginia campus, part of what Data Center Dynamics has called the birthplace of the commercial internet: AOL built the area's first data center, its Dulles Technology Center, in 1997 to support dial-up internet operations, and the fiber infrastructure that project attracted helped trigger the region's growth into Data Center Alley in Loudoun County, now described as the greatest concentration of data center space on the planet at roughly 10 million square feet. Equinix established its own first Ashburn building, DC1, in the late 1990s, and DC2, which followed, has been described by Data Center Dynamics as reputedly the most connected building on earth; Equinix's own published specifications for DC2 describe a single-story, reinforced-concrete, 118,446-square-foot facility with N+1 power redundancy, a minimum cabinet density of 4kVA, 120v/208v power distribution, generators rated for 30 hours or more at full load, N+1 cooling redundancy, a 99.9999%-plus global guaranteed uptime commitment, and certifications including HIPAA, ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, and NIST 800-53/FISMA High. Equinix has continued expanding the Ashburn campus well beyond DC1 and DC2, eventually building out numbered facilities into the twenties as demand grew, with Data Center Frontier reporting on Equinix's plans for a fleet of four-story buildings as part of that expansion. Equinix positions the Ashburn campus as serving one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the US East Coast, offering colocation in private cages, smart-hands support, managed solutions, internet exchange access, metro connectivity, cross-connects, and its own Equinix Fabric and Fabric Cloud Router interconnection products. Equinix's own website confirms this building's address and IBX facility code but, consistent with the rest of Equinix's public site, does not publish this specific building's power capacity or square footage beyond the DC2 example cited above as representative of the campus's general specifications.

reading.body:
Equinix DC5 in Ashburn publishes 57,544 square feet of floor space but discloses no megawatt capacity figure, making its absolute scale unknowable from the operator's own spec page. The facility operates at N+2 power redundancy and N+20% cooling redundancy, which qualifies it for continuous availability workloads but does not indicate the underlying load it supports. Within Virginia's 326 mapped data center facilities, only 23 publish power capacity; DC5 is not among them, and thus does not rank in the state's published megawatt inventory.

DC5 anchors one building in Equinix's 15-facility Washington DC metro region, which the operator positions as North America's largest peering point and a major gateway to Europe. This metro spans Ashburn, Manassas, and Culpeper County, with Ashburn alone hosting twelve of the fifteen facilities. The region's total published capacity across all disclosed sites is 1,375.4 MW, but Equinix does not break this figure by individual building, leaving DC5's contribution opaque.

Without a published megawatt figure, DC5 cannot be assessed for its role in AI scaling against the grid constraint. The facility's participation in the region's capacity is real but quantitatively invisible to this analysis. Prospective tenants or infrastructure investors must request power capacity directly from Equinix, as the spec page provides only redundancy tier and square footage as indicators of scale.
